title: Hartsville Museum

services.name: Dining Room Exhibit
services.desc: Beginning Feb. 1, the newest exhibit at the Hartsville Museum will celebrate Black History Month. The museum’s permanent collection of Black Heritage Stamps and other postal memorabilia will be on display in the W. Reaves McCall Gallery until Feb. 28. USPS' Lena Horne Black Heritage stamp features a 1980s photograph taken by Christian Steiner. The Black Heritage Stamps series first began in 1978, with the 1st honoring abolitionist, Harriet Tubman. The 2018 Black Heritage Stamp, the 41st issuance in the series, honors Lena Horne (1917 - 2010). services.name: Darkside Tours
services.desc: Come along on these fun and interesting tours to learn about some of Hartsville’s “lost” locations and history. Each tour will last approximately 90+ minutes and is suitable for any age at the parent’s discretion. Parking will be available at First Baptist Church and the Hartsville Museum. The cost is $25 per person, plus tax and fees, and will go on sale September 1st. Please note that, while most of the tour will be on our accessible downtown sidewalks, guests will need to use several flights of steps to experience some parts.
